prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Sugar Land, Texas. The claimant was a passenger and reported concussion. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1118; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was stopped in the right lane of the roadway in Sugar Land, Texas, when the rear of Driver 1's vehicle was struck by Driver 2's vehicle, which was following too closely to stop. Driver 2 told me he looked down for a moment and did not see the traffic slowing ahead. Passenger was seated in the front passenger seat of Driver 1's vehicle and reported a concussion, with a headache and dizziness, and was evaluated at the scene before being transported by EMS for further care. Witnesses at the scene, the photographs taken by responding officers, and Driver 2's own account all agree on how the collision happened. The rear bumper and trunk area of Driver 1's vehicle show damage that is largely consistent with the impact described. A few older scratches are visible on the lower bumper, but they may predate this crash and were noted separately. Officers and witnesses confirm that Passenger was in the vehicle at the time of impact. Whether the reported head injury resulted from this collision has not yet been determined. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the policy covering the vehicle.
